title: Losing Holborn and St Pancras is catastrophic for Zack Polanksi
gist: Former YouGov president Peter Kellner argues Labour's Sagal Abdi-Wali defied history by holding Holborn and St Pancras against Green leader Zack Polanski, whose real gain was only 3.5 points despite claims of 'trebling' the vote. Under PM Andy Burnham, Labour has moved from 19% to 29% in polling averages while the combined Green/Lib Dem score fell from 26% to 20%, reducing the Green threat to Labour.

insights.claim: Labour's Sagal Abdi-Wali held Holborn and St Pancras against Green Party leader Zack Polanski, despite a historical average swing of 24 per cent against Labour in government-held seats challenged from the left or centre-left.
insights.speaker: Peter Kellner
insights.so_what: Signals a Labour recovery that lowers UK political fragmentation risk on the left.
insights.quote: The average swing against Labour in such contests was 24 per cent.
insights.locator: Sagal Abdi-Wali has not just defeated

insights.claim: Kellner says the Greens' claim to have trebled their vote is 'paltering': the 2024 left vote was split between the Greens (10.4%) and independent Andrew Feinstein (18.9%), so Polanski's 32.8% was a true increase of just 3.5 points.
insights.speaker: Peter Kellner
insights.so_what: Headline party claims can mislead; adjusted baselines show Green momentum stalled.
insights.quote: Polanski, who won 32.8 per cent: a true increase of just 3.5 percentage points
insights.locator: The Greens can make their “trebling” claim

insights.claim: The Greens' vote in Holborn and St Pancras fell from a combined left-wing 11,342 in 2024 to 8,928 for Polanski, whereas in the February Gorton and Denton byelection it rose from 8,576 to 14,980.
insights.speaker: Peter Kellner
insights.so_what: Green momentum has reversed since February, reducing the threat to Labour's left flank.
insights.quote: the Greens’ record is up more than 6,000 in February, down more than 2,000 in October

insights.claim: Abdi-Wali's vote share fell only 3.7 points on the general election, the best retention of any Labour defender in ten government-era byelections where the main challenge came from the Lib Dems or Greens.
insights.speaker: Peter Kellner
insights.so_what: Historically strong result reinforces evidence of a Labour revival.
insights.locator: Nevertheless, it was no mean achievement

insights.claim: Turnout in Holborn and St Pancras fell from 54 to 39 per cent, so Labour's raw vote also fell, unlike Andy Burnham's Makerfield win where both share and numbers rose.
insights.speaker: Peter Kellner
insights.so_what: Low turnout tempers how much the result signals broad enthusiasm.

insights.claim: Opinium found Zack Polanski's net approval fell from minus seven in February to minus 22, level with Nigel Farage as Britain's least popular party leader.
insights.speaker: Peter Kellner
insights.so_what: Weakening Green leadership reduces fragmentation risk for Labour.

insights.claim: Kellner expects Polanski's reputation to have worsened further after the Green Party voted to define Zionism as racism while he abstained.
insights.speaker: Peter Kellner
insights.so_what: Further Green decline would consolidate the centre-left vote behind Labour.

insights.claim: Averaging five pollsters, Labour has risen from 19% before Andy Burnham became prime minister to 29% now, while the combined Green and Lib Dem score fell from 26% to 20%.
insights.speaker: Peter Kellner
insights.so_what: A recovering Labour government reduces UK political-risk premia tied to fragmentation.
insights.quote: Today, Labour is ahead at 29 per cent, versus a combined Green and Lib Dems score of 20 per cent.

insights.claim: Kellner frames the next UK general election as two separate contests—one to dominate the left and one to dominate the right, where Reform and the Conservatives are currently fighting.
insights.speaker: Peter Kellner
insights.so_what: A split right with a consolidating left favours Labour's prospects of re-election.
insights.quote: It will involve two separate contests, one to dominate the left, the other to dominate the right.

insights.claim: The Lib Dems are de facto Labour allies: in 2024 they gained 60 seats from the Tories and four from the SNP but none from Labour, with only Burnley a Labour-Lib Dem marginal.
insights.speaker: Peter Kellner
insights.so_what: Tactical voting between Labour and Lib Dems is likely to hurt the Conservatives.
insights.locator: Here we should consider the Lib Dems

insights.claim: Kellner argues the Green danger to Labour was siphoning votes needed to fend off Reform and the Tories, and after this byelection the Greens are less likely to be a threat whether or not Polanski stays.
insights.speaker: Peter Kellner
insights.so_what: Lower odds of Reform gains via a split left reduces UK policy-shock risk.
insights.quote: After last night, and whether Polanski stays or goes, the Greens are less likely to be a threat.

insights.claim: Only three times has a Labour government cheered a byelection night as a boost to staying in office: Hull North in 1966, Burnham's Makerfield win four months ago, and Holborn and St Pancras.
insights.speaker: Peter Kellner
insights.so_what: Rare historical pattern supports the thesis of a durable Labour recovery.
insights.locator: Only three times in the party’s history
